assumptions: Different sieve tubes can simultaneously carry opposing directions
Source/sink describes net sugar balance, not fixed organ identity
Loading may use energy; pressure differences drive long-distance bulk flow
limits: No quantitative pressure, water-potential or sugar-transport prediction
Branching, respiration, storage and water exchange omitted from the worked budget
Not opposing simultaneous bulk flows in one sieve tube

L106.type: original qualitative environmental-response and water-balance model

parameters.E: relative water amount per arbitrary time interval; output rounded to 0.1
parameters.uptake: same relative water amount/time as E
parameters.0.4: net water retained for storage/growth per interval in this short-time example; not an instrument correction or universal constant

assumptions: Leaf area and plant identity fixed
One variable changed per fair comparison
Closure retains small residual surface loss except when gradient is zero
Net storage is fixed only for this illustrative interval
limits: No empirical fit or species calibration
Real stomatal feedback and leaf temperature are more complex
Potometer estimates uptake, not direct exact transpiration; leaks and storage matter
Cannot guide plant care or predict absolute flux

parameters.carbon: relative CO2 supply units, selected 40 or 70
parameters.P: relative photosynthetic rate units, not mL oxygen or real carbon fixation
parameters.80: fixed idealised ceiling from remaining controlled conditions

assumptions: Temperature, water, leaf area and measurement interval fixed
Same x-coordinate needed for between-curve CO2 comparisons
Piecewise corners deliberately expose bottleneck logic
limits: Real responses are usually smooth and may involve co-limitation
Relative CO2 supply is not atmospheric ppm
Bubble counts measure a gas proxy affected by volume, dissolution, respiration and gas composition
Short-term relative rate is not harvest yield

L108.type: event checkpoints plus separate mineral-function comparison

checkpoints: pollen transfer from anther to stigma (compatibility not required for pollination)
embryo development; ovule may become seed
mineral_conditions: low N: amino-acid and other synthesis may be limited
low Mg: chlorophyll function may be affected

assumptions: Pollination, fertilisation and seed formation are distinct events
Minerals support function; sugar carbon mainly comes from CO2
limits: Second fusion of double fertilisation and fruit development omitted
Pollen arrival does not guarantee fertilisation or mature seed set
Mineral comparison is not a quantitative seed-count model or a symptom diagnosis
